To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the production of heavy quarks in nucleusnucleus collisions at LHC is very sensitive to the parton distribution function and to the heavy quark mass, and that the evolution of heavy flavors in the quarkgluon plasma can be described by a partonic transport approach, BAMPS.

the production of heavy quarks in nucleusnucleus collisions at the RHIC and LARC energies is strongly dependent on the choice of parton distribution functions and the heavy quark mass, but not significantly affected by the choice of the initial gluon distribution.
the charm production cross section is strongly dependent on the parton density, the charm mass, and the scale of the parton-parton collision.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the space-time dynamics of charm and bottom production within a fully dynamical transport approach.
the production and space-time dynamics of charm and bottom in nucleus-nucleous collisions at RHIC (RH) and LHC (LH) energies.
the space-time evolution of heavy quark production and the production of heavy quarkonia in nucleus-nucleous collisions.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the heavy quark production in the quarkinetic matter can be described within a partonic kinetic approach.

the heavy quark production and space-time dynamics in heavy ion collisions at the RHIC and LAC energies are well described by the partonic transport approach, which is in particular sensitive to the initial gluon conditions and charm mass, while the bottom mass is irrelevant.
the charm production in the QGP at RHIC is negligible, while at the LHC it is not.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have shown that the production and the space-time evolution of heavy quark can be described in a consistent framework, which is based on the Boltzmann approach of multi-parton scatterings (BAMPS).
heavy quarks, produced at the early stage of heavy ion collisions, can be used as probes to study the properties of the hot and dense quark-gluons medium.
the charm production in the QGP is significant at RHIC and even more at LHC.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the production and evolution of heavy quark in the quark gluon plasma is a very sensitive process, and it is very important to get the initial conditions right, in particular the gluon initial condition, and to understand the heavy quark mass and K factors.
charm and bottom production and evolution are very sensitive to the details of the initial conditions and heavy quark production.
heavy quarks, especially charm and bottom, are produced and evolved within a partonic plasma in a fully dynamical way in BAMPS.
